# Informed observing-contract boundary study

These four complete first projects and their hashes are saved before their
first CLI observations. The author is the Codex assistant with repository and
Issue #46 access, the adopted pure `reference(f)` decision, the common checker,
and the existing VM-26 exact history oracle. No external model was invoked.
This is informed contract design, not a blind authoring benchmark.

`control` uses the existing open observing-function API. `pure-reference`
deliberately supplies an observing function to the adopted Unitary-only Meaning
constructor: rejection must remain. The two `apply_contract` projects express
a desired, unadopted extension to the existing call form. Their current rejection
does not establish downstream instrument equality or preservation.

The intended positive equation is Z-readout after H H versus direct Z-readout,
as complete unnormalized maps for both public outcomes and all input/reference
states. The negative nondestructive parity-readout example keeps the input in
the matching branch; replacing it with freshly prepared zero has the same
outcome probabilities but changes the residual state and reference correlations.

A separate exact experiment compares independently authored original programs
by outcome-indexed Choi coefficients. Hidden histories are summed incoherently,
not compared as a canonical Kraus list. It is an untrusted host experiment;
native VM-26 reconstruction and trace-preservation checks are separate evidence,
not a production requested-instrument acceptance gate or a source proof.

These probes use at most two live physical qubits. They do not introduce general
operation arrows, rectangular pure Meaning, QFT implementation, new primitives,
schemas or ledger entries. QS/PR/RS/EXACT and both scoped guarantees retain
their adopted scopes and all broader pending obligations.
